title: premises.json
description: A ledger of the premises a task relies on, each tied to a quoted primary source and to the tests that pin it.

task.description: What the task is, in one line.

testFiles.description: Globs, relative to this file, of the test files that test IDs are searched in.

source.description: An http(s) URL, a local path relative to this file, or git:<ref>:<path> with the path relative to the repository root.

claim.description: The fact the task relies on, in your own words.

source.description: The primary source: the system itself, its docs, or the decision record.

quote.description: A verbatim passage from the source. Only whitespace is normalized.

retrieved.description: The date the quote was read from the source.

verdict.description: What the source says about the claim. Only supported premises may be pinned by tests.

tests.description: IDs of the tests that pin this premise. Each ID must appear verbatim in a file matched by testFiles.

paraphrasedIn.description: Secondary documents that restate the claim, such as a contract or brief. Their quotes are checked, but they never support the claim.

snapshot.description: A stored copy of an http(s) source, used when a live fetch fails, or when jsRendered is true and the live page does not show the quote.

jsRendered.description: True when the source page is rendered by JavaScript, so a successful fetch that lacks the quote falls back to the snapshot. Without it, such a fetch is a missing quote.
